clue.text: Turn out everything after February's turned

indicators.note: turned tells us the abbreviation for the month is read back to front

parts.note: FEB is the usual abbreviation for February
everything means all

explanation.surface: Something happens to everything once February has gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses FEB to BEF, and 'after' puts ALL behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To befall is to happen, so turn out (as events do) is a synonym.

clue.text: A Belgian Nobel prize winner

definitions.meaning: a native of Flanders, the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium
the Scottish scientist who discovered penicillin and won the 1945 Nobel prize for medicine

explanation.surface: A man from Belgium who won a Nobel prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A Fleming is a Flemish-speaking native of Belgium; Alexander Fleming won the Nobel prize for discovering penicillin.

clue.text: William's backers, getting a sign, wander in

indicators.note: in tells us the word for wander goes inside the word for a sign

parts.note: an omen is a sign of what is to come
to range is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: King William's supporters see a portent and drift in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order, Protestant supporters in Northern Ireland, are named after William of Orange, King William III, who won the Battle of the Boyne.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order honour William III, so they are his backers by tradition.

clue.text: Take Latin

parts.note: the clue asks for the Latin word meaning 'take!', the imperative once written at the head of a doctor's prescription

explanation.surface: An instruction to study Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol Rx on prescriptions abbreviates this Latin imperative; the word later came to mean a set of cooking instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is literally the Latin command 'take', which opened medical prescriptions.

clue.text: Feign concern

definitions.meaning: to put on a pretence of something
to have an influence on or involve someone

explanation.surface: Pretend to be worried.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect a manner is to feign it; to affect someone is to concern or influence them.

clue.text: A little 9 across cleric being quite precise

parts.note: 9 across is ACCOUNT, abbreviated in banking to AC (a/c)
a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman keeps a brief but exact record of the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' means a shortened form, so the answer to 9 across is cut to its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being accurate means being exactly right, which is to be quite precise.

clue.text: Fear no more the o'the great." Shakespeare (Cymbe line)

definitions.text: Fear no more the o'the great

parts.words: Fear no more the o'the great
parts.note: a quotation with a word missing, to be filled in from the dirge in Shakespeare's Cymbeline

explanation.surface: A line from a song in Shakespeare's Cymbeline with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'Fear no more the ... o' the great; thou art past the tyrant's stroke': the missing word is a scowl of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap in the quoted line is filled by a word for a stern disapproving look, as the play's text reads.

clue.text: The chairman in opposition never dithers

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: dithers suggests wavering confusion, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A committee head who resists change never hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dithers' jumbles NEVER into VENER, which follows CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A convener calls and chairs a meeting, so is its chairman.

clue.text: A stretcher not used in day light

definitions.text: A stretcher not used in day light

parts.words: A stretcher not used in day light
parts.note: a device that makes pictures bigger, worked in a darkroom because daylight would spoil the paper

explanation.surface: A medical stretcher that stays out of use during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretcher' suggests carrying the injured; here it is a photographic device that stretches an image, and the printing paper must be kept from light.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic enlarger magnifies a negative onto paper in a darkroom, so it stretches images away from daylight.

clue.text: Reckoning to sound like a person of noble status

indicators.note: to sound like signals that the answer is said the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman, so this gives 'a count'

explanation.surface: A calculation that sounds aristocratic.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a reckoning or statement of money owed.

clue.text: A married man in the Middle East

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband living in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a city in the Middle East, the capital of Jordan.
explanation.definitionFit: Amman is the capital of Jordan, a city located in the Middle East.

clue.text: Quiet campanologist accepting golden dish

indicators.note: accepting means the quiet bell-ringer takes the gold inside

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical direction for quiet
a campanologist is a bell-ringer, a ringer
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A hushed bell-ringer receives a gold-plated plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts OR between P and RINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A porringer is a small bowl for porridge or soup, a kind of dish.

clue.text: Some boyhood effort at poetry writing

indicators.note: some signals that only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's early attempt at writing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, a piece of poetry writing.

clue.text: Delayed breaking cover-surprisingly green

indicators.note: breaking means the scrambled colour bursts into the cover

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the colour's letters appear in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone was slowed down after an unexpectedly green surface broke through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' turns GREEN into NGERE, and 'breaking' sets that inside LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingered means stayed on or loitered, so was delayed.

clue.text: A moving experience

parts.note: an emotional event read literally as getting from one place to another

explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like 'touching'; it means going somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel is journeying, literally an experience of movement.

clue.text: To limit alcoholic liquor appears a reasonable solution

parts.note: to ration is to limit supply
ale is beer, an alcoholic liquor

explanation.surface: Cutting back on drink looks like the sensible answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoned basis or explanation for something.

clue.text: Vets' idea for giving a tranquilliser

indicators.note: giving means yielding or bending out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Animal doctors' thinking about administering a calming drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' rearranges VETSIDEA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a drug that calms, the same as a tranquilliser.

clue.text: Vetch is included in animal fodder sometimes

indicators.note: is included in shows the answer is tucked inside the following words

explanation.surface: A plant that farmers sometimes add to animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ers is bitter vetch, a plant grown for fodder, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Ers is the name of the bitter vetch, a leguminous plant.

clue.text: Check the remainder before the wet weather

parts.note: the rest is what remains
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Look at what is left before the rain comes.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back, as in checking a horse.

clue.text: Initially the English aristocracy's drink

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: The beverage first favoured by the English upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot drink.

clue.text: Go and apply for one

parts.note: to beg is to ask or apply for something
taken as written

explanation.surface: Go ahead and request a single item.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command meaning go away.

clue.text: The French love for stars

parts.note: le is the masculine 'the' in French
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Gallic affection for the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the Lion, is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: A woman carrying a child shows such craft

indicators.note: carrying means the woman holds the child inside her name

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman displays a particular skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Freemasonry is called 'the Craft', and masonry is also the stonemason's craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is the stoneworker's trade, and also Freemasonry, known as the Craft.

clue.text: Set a time to make calculations

definitions.note: the clue uses a plural for a rough calculation or reckoning

indicators.note: to make means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fix an appointment for doing the sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges SETATIME into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is a rough calculation of a figure.

clue.text: Poles a Communist trapped

parts.note: S and N, the abbreviations for south and north, the Earth's poles
a red is a Communist

explanation.surface: Polish people and a Communist were caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Snared means caught in a snare, so trapped.

clue.text: Improves the tip in a German town

indicators.note: in tells us the tip goes inside the town's name

parts.note: Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany
the end is the tip of something

explanation.surface: A rubbish tip in Germany gets upgraded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a rubbish dump; it is the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text, which improves it.

clue.text: A pink vehicle-and people will go after it!

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A pink car, and a crowd chases it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' looks like a colour; it is the flower family Dianthus, the pinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnation belongs to the Dianthus family of flowers, known as pinks.

clue.text: When one is upset a row can result

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An argument can break out when someone gets upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A row (rhyming with cow) is a din or loud noise.

clue.text: She demonstrated her distress in returning a medal

indicators.note: returning means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour with a medal

explanation.surface: A woman shows she is upset by handing back an award.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned to a weeping stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobe is the mythical mother whose grief for her children made her the figure of tears.

clue.text: Like corresponding

explanation.surface: Alike and matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar means alike, and also matching or analogous.

clue.text: Hundreds cleared off, it's asserted

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, five hundreds

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: It is claimed that many hundreds were taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles CLEARED into ECLARED, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Declared means stated or proclaimed, so asserted.

clue.text: Nurse goes round the day before running water

indicators.note: goes round means the nurse surrounds the day before

parts.note: SRN is a State Registered Nurse in the UK
the eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: A nurse makes rounds the evening before the water starts running.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is a British river, a body of running water.
